title: India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC): Strategic and Geoeconomic Dimensions
summary: Analysis of the IMEC initiative as an alternative to China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), fostering multimodal transit through green hydrogen and digital infrastructure.
content: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) comprises two corridors: the East Corridor connecting India to the Arabian Gulf and the Northern Corridor connecting the Gulf to Europe. It includes railway, ship-to-rail transit networks, and road transport routes along with electricity cables, clean hydrogen pipelines, and high-speed data cables. It aims to cut transit times between India and Europe by 40% while enhancing supply chain resilience across the Global South.
whyInNews: Recent ministerial meeting in Abu Dhabi finalizing multimodal customs harmonization and digital documentation standards.
background: Unveiled during India's G20 Presidency in 2023 under the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII).
prelimsFacts: IMEC consists of Eastern Corridor (India to Gulf) and Northern Corridor (Gulf to Europe).
Signatories include India, USA, Saudi Arabia, UAE, France, Germany, Italy, and the European Union.
Integrates clean hydrogen pipelines and high-speed subsea optical data cables alongside rail tracks.

challenges: Geopolitical instability in the Red Sea and West Asia
Harmonization of railway gauges and customs clearing across non-contiguous jurisdictions
Private sector mobilization and debt-financing sustainability
governmentInitiatives: Sagarmala Port Modernization on the Western Seaboard (Kandla, JNPT)
National Green Hydrogen Mission export bunkering facilities
wayForward: Establishing an IMEC Secretariat for unified dispute resolution
Leveraging multilateral development banks (MDBs) to de-risk high-capital segments

mcqs.question:
Regarding the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched under the aegis of the G20 Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment.
2. The corridor encompasses only railway and maritime shipping routes, excluding telecommunications and energy pipelines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct (launched at G20 New Delhi Summit 2023). Statement 2 is incorrect because IMEC explicitly incorporates clean hydrogen pipelines, electricity transmission cables, and high-speed optical fiber connectivity alongside rail and maritime routes.

title: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and the National Deep Tech Startup Policy
summary: Cabinet approvals for commercial fabrication units in Dholera and Sanand, advancing indigenous silicon wafer and ATMP capabilities.
content: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) with an outlay of INR 76,000 crore provides 50% fiscal support for setting up Silicon Fab, Display Fab, Compound Semiconductors, and OSAT facilities. The National Deep Tech Startup Policy (NDTSP) complements this by offering patient capital, intellectual property protection, and technology transfer pathways to bridge the lab-to-market valley of death.
whyInNews: Breakthrough in 28nm and 40nm commercial tape-outs and expansion into compound semiconductors (GaN/SiC) for electric vehicles and defense radar.
background: Global semiconductor supply disruptions during 2020-2022 highlighted critical reliance on Taiwan and South Korea, spurring national security imperatives.
prelimsFacts: India Semiconductor Mission is housed under Digital India Corporation (MeitY).
Offers up to 50% fiscal support on pari-passu basis across all technology nodes.
Compound semiconductors (Gallium Nitride, Silicon Carbide) operate at higher voltages and frequencies than traditional silicon.

challenges: High capital intensity (billion-dollar capex per fab) with rapid obsolescence
Intense requirement for ultra-pure water (UPW) and uninterrupted clean electricity
Global competition offering comparable subsidies (US CHIPS Act, EU Chips Act)
governmentInitiatives: Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme for domestic fabless chip design startups
Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme training 85,000 engineers in VLSI and embedded systems
wayForward: Focus on specialized automotive and IoT mature nodes before capital-intensive sub-3nm nodes
Create dedicated semiconductor industrial clusters with plug-and-play chemical supply chains

mcqs.question:
With reference to the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal support of 50% on pari-passu basis is provided for setting up Silicon Fabs across all technology nodes.
2. Gallium Nitride (GaN) is an example of a compound semiconductor widely used in high-power and high-frequency applications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. ISM uniform 50% fiscal support applies across all nodes, and GaN/SiC compound semiconductors enable high efficiency in power electronics, EVs, and radars.

title: Implementation of Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework: Target 3 (30x30) in India
source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
summary: India's updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) integrating Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs).
content: Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) commits nations to conserve at least 30% of terrestrial, inland water, and coastal/marine areas by 2030 ('30x30'). India achieves conservation expansion through protected areas, community reserves, Sacred Groves, and Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs) mapped with local biodiversity management committees.
whyInNews: MoEFCC notified over 150 new terrestrial and marine OECMs, acknowledging community-led conservation outside formal national parks.
background: Adopted at COP15 of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in 2022, replacing the Aichi Biodiversity Targets.
prelimsFacts: Target 3 aims for 30% protection of land and ocean by 2030 ('30x30').
OECMs (Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures) are geographically defined areas that achieve positive biodiversity outcomes outside designated protected areas.
Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) are statutory bodies constituted under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.

challenges: Balancing infrastructure development with contiguous wildlife corridor integrity
Addressing human-wildlife conflict in forest fringe villages
Resource mobilization under the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF)
governmentInitiatives: People's Biodiversity Registers (PBR) digital documentation across gram panchayats
Project Tiger and Project Elephant unified funding corridors
wayForward: Incentivizing agro-ecological farming and community forestry stewardship
Integrating spatial satellite monitoring (Bhuvan/GIS) with local Gram Sabha conservation plans

mcqs.question:
What is the primary objective of the '30x30 target' adopted under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework?
(a) To reduce industrial carbon emissions by 30% by 2030
(b) To protect and conserve at least 30% of Earth's land and ocean area by 2030
(c) To replace 30% of global fossil fuels with biofuels by 2030
(d) To eliminate 30 high-hazard agro-chemicals globally by 2030

options.A: To reduce industrial carbon emissions by 30% by 2030
options.B: To protect and conserve at least 30% of Earth's land and ocean area by 2030
options.C: To replace 30% of global fossil fuels with biofuels by 2030
options.D: To eliminate 30 high-hazard agro-chemicals globally by 2030

mcqs.explanation: Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework commits nations to effectively conserve and manage at least 30% of the world's lands, inland waters, coastal areas and oceans by 2030.
